EMBRACING THE ICONIC TOURIST VIEWPOINTS

Tourist Traditions: Capturing the Overdone and Beloved

There’s something almost absurd about photographing famous landmarks these days.

You arrive to find a crowd of people from around the world, all waiting to take more or less the same picture. You wait your turn, raise your camera, and repeat the ritual, all with another line of impatient people forming behind you. Somewhere in that process, it’s super easy to forget what made the place worth looking at in the first place.

I’m not immune to any of this. The photographs here aren't novel takes (and you could find countless others snapped from the same spots, many of which are much better), but they're my personal attempt to document the wonders of the world from my eyes, and to capture the beauty I saw as something I can recollect for the future.

I like imagining them as part of an unbroken chain of cliché photographs, each preserving a moment in someone else’s life. The same building, bridge, or stretch of water becomes part of the memories of people from little corners of the world who will never meet.

Maybe you’ve stood in one of these spots already. Maybe someday you’ll arrive, raise your camera, and take almost exactly the same picture. We’ll have stood in the same place, looking at the same thing, years apart.

The photograph may be familiar, but the moment was mine. And someday, it might be yours as well. How cool would that be?
